sections.content: How many people are "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators"?

58,655 people

were counted on the census as "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators operate and assist with still, cine and television cameras, operate other equipment to record, manipulate and project sound and vision for entertainment, cultural, commercial and industrial purposes, and operate drones to provide aerial video and photographs.

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators", 15.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators" included:

  • fitness and wellbeing instructors
  • interior designers
  • engineering professionals (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators" there were more men than women (70.9% compared with 29.1%).

This means "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "culture, media and sports occupations".

Men made up 70.9% and women made up 29.1% of "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators" included:

  • estimators, valuers and assessors
  • clergy
  • upholsterers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "photographers, audio-visual and broadcasting equipment operators", 10.2% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (55.5% compared with 44.5%).

They are also more likely to be self-employed (63.8%) than an employee (36.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Hackney, this is in the same region of London.
